policy: Blocking calls inside `async fn` that are accepted, keyed by `file::fn`. Every entry must state the *phase* that makes it safe: these functions run before the listener accepts connections or after it stops serving, so the blocking call cannot delay a request. A new blocking call inside an allow-listed function is still accepted (the reason describes the function, not one line) — keep such functions strictly phase-bound. Remove an entry when the site disappears; the gate reports stale entries. **One cause can produce two lines of output** (REQ-A454, measured): a refactor that moves the site into a *differently named* function (`serve` → wrappers + `…_full`) leaves the old key naming a function that no longer holds it ⇒ the gate prints the site as unexpected **and** the old key as stale, and a reader who fixes only one of the two is still red. When the gate says both, the fix is one edit: re-key the entry onto the function that holds the sites today, and re-verify the reason against that body (a reason is about a *function*, so it must be re-read after the function changes).

sites.crates/amos-ai/src/main.rs::main: Daemon startup: removes a stale unix-socket file before `serve` binds. Runs before a single connection is accepted.
sites.crates/amos-ai/src/server.rs::serve_with: Bind-time socket permission hardening (`std::fs::set_permissions(…, 0o700)`, REQ-A141) — it runs immediately after `UnixListener::bind` and **before** the accept task is spawned, so it cannot delay a request. The reason used to also cover post-shutdown socket removal; REQ-A451 moved that half into the **sync** `remove_socket()` helper (a plain `fn`, so the gate no longer sees it, and this entry no longer needs to claim it).
sites.crates/amos-translate/src/lib.rs::serve: Same startup/shutdown pair as the AI daemon: socket hardening while binding, socket removal after the loop exits.
sites.crates/amos-translate/src/main.rs::main: Translate-daemon startup: stale socket cleanup before binding.
sites.crates/amos-mdm/src/admin_auth.rs::requi: Not a call at all, and recorded here rather than reworded away: the single `std::net::` token in this async middleware is a **type** in the refusal log line — `ConnectInfo<std::net::SocketAddr>` from the request extensions. It opens no socket, resolves nothing and blocks on nothing; the token is the scanner's textual marker for a class of real defects (a blocking network call on the runtime), and this site is the false-positive end of that class.
